theorem.forward: for connected canonical F and a coherent b-pin assignment with nonterminal raw cofactor: erased free identities e<=2min(k0,k1), retained identities r>=n-2b, components c<=1+5b, and largest component L>=ceil((n-2b)/(1+5b))
theorem.inverse: if every nonterminal residual component has at most M source identities then b>=ceil((n-M)/(2+5M))
theorem.power_corollary: for M=floor(n^lambda), fixed 0<lambda<1, the restricted pin depth is Omega(n^(1-lambda)); this is not an arbitrary-machine lower bound
theorem.wrapper_firewall: a source-faithful raw-cofactor wrapper below that depth must either be terminal or leave a component larger than M; a semantic/noninjective reencoder is outside the theorem
